counterfactual_missing_items: No hyper-intense signals in diffusion-weighted images
No vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis
decisive_items: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons
Significantly decreased amplitude of right facial nerve compound muscular action potential compared to healthy side
response.rationale: R6 best integrates the pontine lesion with ipsilateral lower-motor-neuron facial nerve damage on ENoG/EMG and non-ischemic MRI features. R4 is a less specific neoplastic label, while R8 captures only the clinical syndrome. R5 is contradicted by absent DWI restriction and patent vertebrobasilar arteries; R1 lacks electrophysiologic and temporal support for demyelination.

rejected.why: Pontine lesion alone is nonspecific; no dissemination in time/space, CSF, or DWI/electrophysiologic support for MS.
Neuroma is a less specific neoplastic label and does not account for the facial nerve CMAP/EMG pattern as precisely as facial nerve schwannoma.
Contradicted by no DWI hyperintensity and no vertebrobasilar artery occlusion or stenosis.
Peripheral facial palsy is a clinical syndrome, not the underlying pontine lesion, and ignores the MRI and ENoG/EMG evidence.
